title: Finite spectrum of a finite-type field algebra forces maximal primes
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $B$ be a commutative $k$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], allowing $B=0$. If $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has finitely many prime ideals, then every prime ideal of $B$ is maximal (equivalently, $\dim B\le0$).

source.place: Lemma 0ALW (finite type algebra with finitely many prime ideals), equivalence of (1) and (2)

proof.text: Use Mathlib’s finite-type characterization of quasi-finiteness. Since the whole prime spectrum is finite, every fiber over a prime of the field is finite, so `Algebra.QuasiFinite.iff_finite_comap_preimage_singleton` gives `Algebra.QuasiFinite k B`. The prime spectrum of a field is discrete, and `Algebra.QuasiFinite.discreteTopology_primeSpectrum` therefore gives a discrete topology on `PrimeSpectrum B`. Applying `PrimeSpectrum.discreteTopology_iff_finite_and_krullDimLE_zero` yields `Ring.KrullDimLE 0 B`; finally `Ring.krullDimLE_zero_iff` gives `p.IsMaximal`.

proof_origin.place: Finite spectrum implies quasi-finite, then discrete spectrum and Krull dimension zero
